question: In normal female puberty, the growth spurt typically occurs BEFORE breast development (thelarche).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. In girls, thelarche (Tanner B2) is the FIRST event of puberty, and the peak height velocity (growth spurt) occurs at B2–B3 — early in puberty, not before it. This contrasts with boys, in whom the growth spurt occurs later.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the growth spurt does NOT precede thelarche. In girls, thelarche (Tanner B2) marks the onset of puberty and the growth spurt occurs at B2–B3, after breast development has begun.
